title: Fractal Econ Field Lab: sprint log for batching + cache + quantization
creator: Asha Patel
description: Run a compact, hypothesis-driven field lab to measure joint benefits and regression risks when applying adaptive batching, KV-prefetch cache policies, and int8 quantization to production-like workloads. Deliver concrete rollout decision criteria, cost savings model, and observability dashboards to support safe canarying across Dedicated and Hosted tiers.
milestones: Shadow traffic run on staging with observability (2025-01-31)
Live canary (10% traffic) on low-risk routes (2025-02-18)
okrs: O: Reduce average token cost for targeted routes
KR1: Achieve >=18% token-cost reduction on test routes vs baseline
KR2: p99 latency degradation <= 8ms on canaried requests
KR3: No customer-facing quality regressions above threshold on prompt set (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding similarity)
workstreams: Quality regressions and eval sets (Research + Product)
risks: Quantization introduces subtle quality regressions on long-context prompts
Aggressive batching can increase tail latency spikes during traffic bursts
Cache staleness or incorrect KV prefetch may leak customer-specific state if misconfigured
Metrics noise may mask small regressions during short canaries
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end harness reproduces production distribution within +/-10% token-length profile
Observability surfaces token-econ, latency, and quality signals within single dashboard
Canary run demonstrates >=18% cost savings without violating p99 latency or quality thresholds
Runbook includes automated rollback and manual mitigation steps and is approved by SRE
updates: 2025-01-12: Kickoff meeting; aligned on target routes and initial eval prompts. Action: Eng to instrument replay harness.
2025-01-22: Synthetic replay validated against 3 sample routes; batch scheduler parameter grid defined; research drafted quantization checklist.
2025-02-02: Shadow run on staging for 72h completed. Observability metrics show early 15% tokens_per_gpu_hour improvement with 3ms median latency increase.
2025-02-18: Canary started at 10% traffic for route set A; automated rollback hooks in place; devops on-call notified.
2025-02-24: Canary expanded to 25% on low-risk routes after no quality regressions detected in sample prompts; cost model updated with real traffic mix.
2025-02-28: Post-canary analysis in progress; preliminary savings 19% on canaried traffic; p99 latency +6ms; next steps: finalize rollout playbook and schedule wider ramp in Cycle 2025-W09.
